$comment: Documents of the Magisterium that vatican.va does not publish, and that
this corpus's own apparatus names. The tracked tier of the map —
`build/magisterium-map/` derives everything else from the indexes in
raw/, and this is the part no page can regenerate, because there is no
page (root CLAUDE.md, 'Output regenerable only from a previous copy of
itself is not regenerable').
WHAT PUTS AN ENTRY HERE. `cited` is how many of the corpus's 132,979
citation strings name the document by kind and title — `Bull
Ineffabilis Deus`, `Enc. Quanta cura` — and match nothing the map lists
and nothing build/ holds. It is a measurement, so it carries the day it
was taken; it is evidence for the claim beside it, not an inventory
number, and it will move as the corpus grows.
WHAT DOES NOT BELONG HERE. A document vatican.va publishes in a family
this map does not cover is NOT missing from vatican.va — `Dominicae
Cenae` is cited 21 times and sits under `letters/`, which is a
different question and a different answer. Nor does a spelling the
apparatus varies (`Ad coeli reginam` for `ad-caeli-reginam`,
`Sollecitudo` for `Sollicitudo`); those are ours to normalise.
FIELDS: title, document_kind, pontiff_or_council, promulgated (ISO, or
the year alone where the day is not established), cited, measured, and
note — why vatican.va has no page. No source is named: finding the text
elsewhere is a separate decision under `docs/decisions.md` §Scope, and
this file's job is to say what is missing, not to go and get it.

documents.title: Unam Sanctam
documents.note: vatican.va's papal shell begins at Leo XIII; it publishes nothing of Boniface VIII.

documents.title: Apostolici Regiminis
documents.note: The councils mirror carries the First and Second Vatican Councils and no earlier one.

documents.title: Ineffabilis Deus
documents.note: Pius IX has no document index on vatican.va. The most-cited document in this file, and the definition of the Immaculate Conception.

documents.title: Quanta Cura
documents.note: Pius IX has no document index on vatican.va. The Syllabus of Errors was issued with it and is cited in the corpus as `DS` rather than by title.
